text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Court role goes to PQ stalwart: Over province's objections, sovereignist lawyer to argue for Quebec in Charter case
-Tribunal gives Serb 20-year sentence: War crimes panel focus of anger
-Stepparents in child-suppport limbo: Supreme Court urged to clarify financial obligations in cases of divorce
-Moonlighting triples in 20 years: Need for mulitiple jobs reflects loss of employment security, Statscan study says
-Breast cancer activists issue call for action: Environmental causes of disease ignored in favour of genetic research, delegates say
-Asper hands over the reins: CanWest chairman makes Peter Viner, one of his top executives, the broadcaster's CEO
-Canadians work overtime-for free: One-fifth of employees put in extra hours in first quarter; about 60% unpaid, Statscan finds
-MacLellan rejects Sable deal: Nova Scotia's premier-designate wants pipeline tolls changed

-Solv-Ex seeks creditor protection: Plunging shares hobble financing THE FINANCIAL POST: -Solv-Ex declared insolvent: Company blocks access to its controversial north Alberta oilsands project, files for bankruptcy protection here and says it may seek Chapter 11 in U.S. -Canada balks at open door for foreign banks
